meta.title: Where should this workload run?
meta.description: A decision tree for cloud hosting: five questions about how the code runs and is packaged lead to functions, containers, an app platform or virtual machines.

summary.headline: Pick the most managed option that fits; drop a level only for a concrete reason.
points: Short event-driven jobs go to functions; long ones to batch containers.
A handful of containerised services suit serverless containers; Kubernetes pays off only with a platform team.
Virtual machines are for software that needs the operating system or a licence tied to it.

data.title: How does the code run?
data.subtitle: Always on, or triggered by events

data.title: Functions
data.subtitle: Pay per call, scale to zero
data.description: Queue consumers, webhooks and scheduled tasks. Watch cold starts on user-facing paths.

data.title: Batch containers
data.subtitle: Jobs that run for hours
data.description: Nightly imports, video encoding, model training. Use spot capacity where the job can restart.

data.title: Already packaged as containers?
data.subtitle: A Dockerfile that builds and runs

data.title: Virtual machines
data.subtitle: You patch the operating system
data.description: Use an autoscaling group built from a hardened image; never hand-built servers.

data.title: App platform
data.subtitle: Push code, the platform runs it
data.description: Simplest for a web app or API in a mainstream language; containerise later if needed.

data.title: Over 10 services and a platform team?
data.subtitle: People to run a cluster

data.title: Managed Kubernetes
data.subtitle: Shared cluster per environment
data.description: Worth it at scale for shared networking, policy and tooling, but needs people who own the cluster.

data.title: Serverless containers
data.subtitle: Run a container, no cluster
data.description: Scales per request, including to zero; no nodes to upgrade.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Start at the top. Green options are fully managed, teal run containers for you, orange leave more to your team. The event-driven branch opens folded; the steps unfold it.

steps.title: Event-driven work
steps.description: Code that runs when something happens: short runs fit functions, long jobs need batch containers.

steps.title: Always-on services
steps.description: For an API or web app, the next question is whether it already ships as a container.

steps.title: Not containerised
steps.description: Software that needs the operating system goes on virtual machines; everything else is easiest on an app platform.

steps.title: Containers: cluster or not
steps.description: Kubernetes pays off with many services and a team to run it. A few services run more cheaply as serverless containers.
